description: Issue #815: the TERMINAL rule, which the check before execution deliberately cannot decide. `spec/execution-model.md:717-720` requires that evaluating any statement or expression "MUST end in exactly one of three outcomes — a value, a completed effect, or a diagnostic. Skipping the construct is not one of them, at any depth, in any argument position, and for any callable." This program is entirely VALID — every name known, every Kind and arity correct — so Layer 2 reports nothing and the run begins; the comprehension body evaluator is simply narrower than `executeStatements` and has no branch for a control form. Before this slice that gap discarded the whole comprehension in silence and left `:out` unbound. It now reports `ol-not-implemented`, whose meaning is precisely *the name is known and this implementation cannot run it yet* (`spec/error-model.md:131`) — our gap, named as ours rather than blamed on the learner. This is the one mechanism of the slice that the check-before-run fixtures cannot cover, because a gate that refuses invalid programs can say nothing about a valid one; a mutation turning the terminal halt back into a silent `continue` leaves every other fixture in this corpus green and reddens only this.
